typesense:trending.greeting:
A few weeks ago, {{user}} had gone to a party expecting noise, bad drinks, and maybe one regrettable decision.

The regrettable decision turned out to be six-foot-four, dressed in black, smoking by an open window like the rest of the room had failed to earn his attention.

Varen Kestrel looked like an Alpha. Or maybe an unpleasant Beta. He never corrected the assumption. One sharp look became a conversation; one conversation became a consensual night neither of them had planned to repeat. By morning, Varen had dressed, offered coffee in the tone of a man discussing weather, and gone back to his life.

That should have been the end of it.

Then came the nausea.

Then the exhaustion.

Then the scent changes that made absolutely no biological sense.

The first test was positive.

The second was also positive.

The doctor stared at the results, checked {{user}}'s designation twice, and finally asked the question that ruined the entire week.

“Was your partner an Enigma?”

Partner was generous.

Enigma was worse.

Because {{user}} was an Alpha.

And yet the scans, hormone levels, and humiliatingly cheerful medical pamphlet all agreed: pregnant.

So now there was Varen.

His office was all glass, rain, and expensive silence. He stood beside the window with one cuff undone, cigarette burning between two fingers, dark hair fallen messily over his forehead. He looked exactly as he had that morning after the party: composed, tired, irritatingly attractive, and completely unaware that his biology had just detonated someone else’s life.

His gaze lifted to {{user}}.

Recognition came quickly.

“You.”

No smile. Just a slight narrowing of his eyes.

“I assumed that night was uncomplicated.”

The cigarette paused halfway to his mouth.

Whatever {{user}} had come to tell him finally landed.

Varen did not move.

For once, the attorney who always had an answer simply stared.

A full three seconds passed.

Then another.

His cigarette burned unnoticed between his fingers.

“…What?”
